    Robot Presets¶

    Robot presets are RobotOptions subclasses with the asset, DOF order, PD gains, armature and limits of one robot already filled in; construct one and put it in a scene. Composite rigs bundle several presets (an arm and a gripper, a humanoid and two hands) into one validated options object. The robots guide covers the catalog, composite rigs and adding a robot.

    import eden as en
from eden.options.robots import COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY, ROBOT_REGISTRY, Droid

robot = en.robots.Go1()
rig = Droid(base_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.4))           # hand-less Panda + Robotiq 2F-85
cls = COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY.get("ur5e_2f85")  # -> UR5eRobotiq

    ROBOT_REGISTRY looks unit robots up by key and COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY composite rigs. Each section below renders one module of eden.options.robots.

    Humanoids¶

    Unitree G1¶

    Unitree G1 humanoid configurations (23/29 DOF variants).

    23-active-DOF G1 built from the 29-DOF G1 with wrists welded (the AMO / GMT training robot).

    G1Dofs29Dex3 ¶

    G1Dofs29Dex3(**data)

    Bases: G1Dofs29

    Unitree G1 29DoF + two 7-DOF Dex3 hands (43 actuated DOFs) — the SONIC teleop sim body.

    Body joints keep the :class:G1Dofs29 actuator spec. Hand gains are the Dex3 controller's values (kp 1.5 / kd 0.1, dex3_hands.hpp); hand armature and force limits come from the source MJCF (armature 0.01, actuatorfrcrange ±2.45 thumb base / ±1.4 other fingers).

    The MJCF is the GEAR-SONIC model, kept separate from g1_29dof_rev_1_0: the SONIC calibration offsets are pinned to this model's torso_link frame (10 mm lower than rev_1_0's). file is the single source of truth for the asset path — the operator-side FK and visualizer read it too.

    OliNoHands ¶

    OliNoHands(**data)

    Bases: Oli

    Oli with its moulded rubber hands removed, for welding a real end effector.

    Teleoperating a Dex3 / XHand / Dex1 gripper (or a Wuji Hand2 — see :class:~eden.options.robots.composite.oli_wuji.OliWuji) means welding that end effector onto the wrist, and the stock moulded hand would then sit stacked inside it. This variant points at HU_D04_01_no_hand.urdf; every joint and every other link is identical to the stock URDF, so DOFs, gains and pose are inherited unchanged from :class:Oli. Four things differ:

    • *_wrist_roll_link points at *_wrist_roll_link_nohand.STL. This is what removes the hand: it is baked into the stock wrist mesh, not carried on a link, and so is the silver end-cap it bolted onto. Dropping both leaves 72 of 322 cm^3 and exposes the real flange.
    • The wrist inertial is recomputed for the bare metal — 0.205 kg with its CoM 2.9 cm down, against the stock 0.581 kg at 8.9 cm, which was dominated by the rubber hand. So the arm carries the end effector you weld on, not that plus a phantom 0.38 kg per wrist.
    • Two *_hand_mount frames are added on the exposed flange (z = -0.058 in *_wrist_roll_link, the plane upstream's own stock URDF puts *_hand_contact on). They carry no mass and no geometry; welding an end effector to them needs no offset.
    • The four fixed *_hand_{manip,contact} links/joints are dropped. Despite the names these are not the hand, just 1 cm / 1 g marker boxes for the grasp and contact frames LimX's stack targets; they are fixed children Genesis merges away regardless.

    PhcSmplHumanoid ¶

    PhcSmplHumanoid(**data)

    Bases: SmplHumanoid

    PHC's phc_3 SMPL humanoid: neutral shape, upright start, box body, real weight, PD-driven.

    The :class:SmplHumanoid skeleton (same bodies, joints, geoms and DOF order) generated with the robot options PHC trained phc_3 with (real_weight_porpotion_boxes=True, so the five box geoms carry their real-weight densities instead of 1000) and with the floor, light and motors stripped (examples/projects/mimic/assistmimic/scripts/generate_smpl_xml.py). Isaac Gym read each joint's stiffness / damping as a position drive and the motor gear as its effort limit; here they are default_dofs_kp / default_dofs_kd (calibrated for Genesis by PHC_DRIVE_K*_SCALE) and default_dofs_force_limits, and the passive spring and damper are zeroed.

    Franka Emika Panda and Franka Research 3¶

    Franka Emika Panda and Franka Research 3 arm configurations.

    Attributes¶

    Classes¶

    FrankaResearch3 ¶

    FrankaResearch3(**data)

    Bases: RobotOptions

    The Franka Research 3, Franka Robotics' successor to the Panda.

    From MuJoCo Menagerie's franka_fr3 (Apache-2.0), which derives it from Franka's own franka_description, with two Eden edits baked into the shipped asset: its links and joints are renamed link0…link7 / joint1…joint7 (the naming every other arm here uses, and what this class's DOF maps and the composite rigs address), and the bare attachment_site becomes an attachment body carrying the same mount frame as panda_nohand.xml — 0.107 m up from link7, rotated 135 degrees about z — so a gripper welds onto either Franka arm unchanged.

    The FR3 is the same arm mechanically as the Panda (identical link frames, identical collision hulls, 855 mm reach, 3 kg payload, ±87 / ±12 N·m joint torques), and differs in what it declares: its own joint limits (A6 is shifted by 26 degrees, so a Panda home pose is not automatically reachable), Franka's published inertials, and joint friction identified in torque control (armature 0.195 / 0.074, damping 0.21, frictionloss 1.137 … 0.248) where the Panda model has none.

    FrankaEmikaPandaNoHand ¶

    FrankaEmikaPandaNoHand(**data)

    Bases: RobotOptions

    The Panda arm without its hand: panda_nohand.xml, the seven joints ending in a flange.

    The Panda counterpart of :class:FrankaResearch3, and what a composite rig wants when the end-effector is a separate entity — :class:~eden.options.robots.FrankaEmikaPanda is one MJCF with the fingers inside it, so its hand cannot be swapped or welded to. The two arms expose the same attachment mount frame, so a gripper written for one mounts on the other unchanged.

    The Panda's own gains and joint limits, which are not the FR3's: see :class:FrankaResearch3 for what differs between the two robots.

    OmniReset UR5e rig¶

    UWLab's OmniReset rig: a calibrated UR5e carrying a Robotiq 2F-85 with a D415 mount.

    Converted once from UWLab's USD (UW-Lab/uwlab-assets), which Genesis cannot load: the gripper's parallel linkage is a PhysX articulation with two parents per inner knuckle, coupled by physxMimicJoint constraints. The MJCF rebuilds it as a tree. Each body is placed from its PhysX joint frames at q = 0, so every joint reads PhysX's coordinate; the five mimic joints become joint equalities and the two loop-closing joints are dropped. One authored gearing is corrected: right_inner_knuckle_joint says -1, but its hinge is flipped relative to its mirror, which opens a 72 mm gap in the right finger's loop when closed; +1 closes it to 0.08 mm, and it matches Isaac Lab's recorded states, which read that joint as -finger_joint. Kinematics match UWLab's calibrated analytic model (uwlab_assets.robots.ur5e_robotiq_gripper.kinematics) to 1e-7 m; joint values are PhysX's, so a pose reads what Isaac Lab reports for it.

    One asset rather than a ManipulatorOptions composite of :class:UR5e and :class:Robotiq2f85, because neither part is the same robot: UR5e carries rounded nominal link lengths, putting its flange 1.2 mm (max 2.3 mm) from this calibrated one across random poses — the size of OmniReset's 2.5 mm success tolerance — and Robotiq2f85 is MuJoCo Menagerie's loop-closed 2F-85 (other joints, pad-only colliders, sub-millisecond substeps, no D415 mount), not the mimic linkage whose six joint angles the policy observes.

    Inertials are PhysX's. The arm links' are authored in the USD; the gripper links have none, so the ones here are what Isaac Sim 6.1 derives for UWLab's robot (measured), including 1 kg on each collider-less outer knuckle. With them the arm's mass matrix matches PhysX's to 0.01 %, and UWLab's 120 Hz explicit controller is stable.

    The dynamics are UWLab's implicit-actuator training/eval configuration (IMPLICIT_UR5E_ROBOTIQ_2F85): the arm is torque-driven by an operational-space controller (kp = kd = 0 here; efforts capped at 150/28 N·m), the gripper's finger_joint is a PD servo (kp 17, kd 5, 60 N·m) and the five passive linkage joints follow it through joint equalities. Every link floats (disable_gravity in the USD), which gravity compensation reproduces, and no DOF carries armature or friction — the USD authors none and the stage-1 policy never had the sysid values the finetune stage randomizes.

    Robotiq 2F-85¶

    Robotiq 2F-85 parallel-jaw gripper configuration.

    Attributes¶

    Classes¶

    Robotiq2f85 ¶

    Robotiq2f85(**data)

    Bases: RobotOptions

    Robotiq 2F85 parallel-jaw gripper, tuned for stable grasping.

    The 2F85 is an underactuated four-bar linkage: MuJoCo closes it with <equality><connect> constraints and drives it through a <tendon> actuator. Genesis has no runtime tendon (the actuator is approximated per driver joint at parse time) and solves the loop closures softly, so the stock asset penetrates/oscillates instead of pinching. These options bake in the validated compensation (tuned by SpaceMouse-teleop A/B against the loop-free Franka Hand; pinned by the grasp-and-lift regression in tests/options/robots/test_robotiq_2f85.py):

    • Pads: flat box collision geoms with high friction (a face contact that resists rotation), instead of the original 5-sphere cluster. Pair with collision_link_patterns=[".*pad"] so only the pads collide and the object isn't wedged against the inner linkage.
    • Drive (default_dofs_force_limits): the kp=100 servo commanded to the closed target would develop ~40 N·m and crush through a small object; the cap reproduces MuJoCo's tendon forcerange -5 5 × wrap coef 0.485 = 2.4 N·m per driver.
    • Loop closure (default_equalities_sol_params): the connects + driver coupling are stiffened to near-rigid so grip force transmits through the four-bar to the pads instead of flexing it.
    • Contact (default_geoms_sol_params): pad contact stiffened to match. Genesis mixes a pair's params as the mean of its two geoms (geom priority is ignored), so graspable objects should carry comparable sol params via their own default_geoms_sol_params — never via a global EnvOptions.constraint_timeconst, which over-stiffens every rigid contact and ejects mesh objects on contact.
    • Spring preload (default_dofs_spring_ref): Genesis drops MJCF springref; re-anchoring the spring-link springs at 2.62 rad restores the preload that keeps the passive pad chain taut.
    • Dissipation (damping/frictionloss/armature): at contact the drivers are torque-saturated, so kp/kd have no authority over contact chatter; always-on joint damping (~critical for the pinch mode) and a dry frictionloss stick band absorb it instead.

    Full constraint stiffness needs an effective substep dt <= 0.001 (e.g. sim_dt=0.004, sim_substeps=4); Genesis clamps solref timeconst to 2*substep_dt otherwise.

    Inspire RH56¶

    Inspire RH56 dexterous hands (left/right): the stock RH56 and the RH56DFQ variant Unitree mounts on the G1.

    Both are the same hand: link tree, joint frames and axes, and every link's inertial (0.1918 kg in all) are identical. What differs is the asset each is published with, and so the joint ranges, the coupling ratios and the meshes:

    ========================== ================================== ========================================= asset InspireRH56_* InspireRH56DFQ_* (Weave's G1 rig) ========================== ================================== ========================================= finger proximal range 0 – 1.47 rad 0 – 1.7 rad thumb distal range 0 – 0.4 rad 0 – 1.2 rad couplings URDF <mimic> (Genesis equality) software, via mimic_dofs (no tags) thumb int. / distal ratio 1.334 / 0.667 1.6 / 2.4 finger intermediate ratio 1.06399, offset -0.04545 1.0 ========================== ================================== =========================================

    Six of the twelve joints are mimic followers of the six drivers (actuated_dofs_name). metadata.mimic_dofs publishes the couplings as follower -> (driver, multiplier, offset) for both. The RH56 asset keeps its <mimic> tags, so Genesis couples its followers itself and the mapping is descriptive; the DFQ asset has them stripped, and a task passes the mapping to the joint PD action term, which then commands each follower at driver_target * multiplier + offset (Weave's MimicJointPositionAction)::

    ImplicitPDController.configure(entity_name="left_hand", dofs_name=InspireRH56DFQ_L.actuated_dofs_name,
                               mimic_dofs=InspireRH56DFQ_L.metadata.mimic_dofs)

    Wuji Hand 1¶

    Wuji Hand 1 dexterous hand configurations (left/right, full-mesh or primitive collision).

    Twenty-DOF anthropomorphic hand from Wuji Technology (5 fingers x 4 DOF) with a silicone pad on the thumb -- the hand/body-with-soft package, i.e. the hand the upstream in-hand cube-reorientation RL task (wuji-technology/wuji-mjlab) is built around. The successor generation is :mod:eden.options.robots.wuji_hand2beta2; the two are different hands, not variants (different link names, joint names and kinematics).

    Two collision flavours per side:

    • WujiHand1_{R,L} -- one full visual mesh per link, reused as the collision mesh. Genesis convexifies each, so the palm becomes a single convex hull that bulges over the finger sockets. Fine for visualization, retargeting and teleop.
    • WujiHand1Simplified_{R,L} -- primitive collision (cylinder + end spheres on the proximal links, simplified meshes for the palm, the thumb pad and the five distal links). This reproduces the collision model the upstream MJCF -- and therefore the upstream RL task -- was tuned against, and is much cheaper at thousands of envs. Use this flavour for contact-rich manipulation.

    Assets (URDF + STL meshes, MIT-licensed) live under hands/wuji_hand1 in the Kashu7100/eden_assets dataset, converted from the upstream wuji-technology/wuji-description hand/body-with-soft package.

    Not to be confused with the older, unreferenced hands/wuji_hand directory in the same dataset: that is the upstream hand/body package at v1.0.1 -- same kinematics, but no thumb pad, no simplified-collision flavour, unprefixed link/joint names, and looser joint limits and effort ceilings. Nothing in Eden loads it.

    Composite robots¶

    A composite is a CompositeEntityOptions: it round-trips through the config system and is added to a scene by name like any other entity, and the scene expands it into its unit robots plus the welds that join them. It exposes the controller metadata as properties (arm_dofs on every arm rig, plus gripper_dofs, gripper_open, gripper_close, ... on a ManipulatorOptions and hand_dofs on a DexManipulatorOptions; robot_dofs, left_hand_dofs, right_hand_dofs on a humanoid rig). ManipulatorOptions carries a two-finger gripper, DexManipulatorOptions a dexterous hand, and HumanoidOptions one end-effector per wrist.

    Composite base classes¶

    Base options for composite robots (an arm + an attached gripper, and kin).

    A composite robot bundles several unit-robot :class:RobotOptions into one rig that a scene expands into its constituent entities + welds. Unlike the unit robots in eden/options/robots, a composite is itself a validated Options (a :class:~eden.options.entities.CompositeEntityOptions), so it round-trips through the config system, can declare its own fields, and is added to a scene by name like any other entity::

    from eden.options.robots import Droid

droid = Droid(base_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.4))
scene = en.scenes.Empty(is_support_enabled=True, robot=droid)   # -> robot (arm) + gripper + weld
# ...the same object exposes the controller metadata as shortcut properties:
DifferentialIKController.configure(entity_name=droid.arm_name,
                                   ee_link_name=droid.ee_link,
                                   dofs_name=droid.arm_dofs)

    Two end-effector cases share one arm base (:class:_ArmCompositeOptions): :class:ManipulatorOptions bolts on a two-finger gripper (the manipulator); :class:DexManipulatorOptions bolts on a multi-DOF dexterous hand. Concrete rigs (Franka + Robotiq, UR5e, Franka + XHand, …) subclass one of these with default fields and register in :data:COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY. A humanoid carrying an end-effector per wrist is the third shape, :class:HumanoidOptions — a sibling of the arm base rather than a subclass, because its root is a humanoid with two welds instead of an arm with one (see :mod:eden.options.robots.composite.oli_wuji). mjlab attaches the end-effector to each arm at a tool frame via with_gripper; Eden's equivalent is the scene attachments_dict, which the composite fills in from :meth:expand.

    tcp_offset property ¶
    tcp_offset: tuple[float, float, float]

    The tool point — pad midpoint with the gripper open — in the ee_link frame (m).

    The gripper's own tcp_offset (declared in its base-link frame) carried through the mounting pose the weld applies, so a rig with an attach_offset / attach_quat reports the point where the pads actually are. The config-time twin of the grasp frame the robosuite terms measure on the built rig.

    max_substep_dt property ¶
    max_substep_dt: float | None

    Finest substep either half of the rig needs (None when neither declares one).

    A rig is only as stiff as its stiffest constraint allows: welding a Robotiq onto an arm that imposes nothing still means the rig cannot be stepped above the Robotiq's limit. Read it when choosing EnvOptions.sim_dt / sim_substeps for a scene that holds the rig.

    Methods:¶

    hold_width ¶
    hold_width(width: float, clearance: float = 0.002) -> dict[str, float]

    Finger DOF targets that put the pads width + 2 * clearance apart.

    Linear between gripper_open (pads :attr:stroke apart) and gripper_close (pads touching), clamped to that range — so a Franka Hand holding a 4 cm peg gets each prismatic finger at ~2.2 cm, and a Robotiq the matching driver angle. Meant for objects welded to the hand; a free object is grasped by the gripper action instead.

    def hold_width(self, width: float, clearance: float = 0.002) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Finger DOF targets that put the pads ``width + 2 * clearance`` apart.

    Linear between ``gripper_open`` (pads :attr:`stroke` apart) and ``gripper_close`` (pads
    touching), clamped to that range — so a Franka Hand holding a 4 cm peg gets each prismatic
    finger at ~2.2 cm, and a Robotiq the matching driver angle. Meant for objects welded to the
    hand; a free object is grasped by the gripper action instead.
    """
    closed = min(max(1.0 - (width + 2.0 * clearance) / self.stroke, 0.0), 1.0)
    return {
        dof: self.gripper_open[dof] + closed * (self.gripper_close[dof] - self.gripper_open[dof])
        for dof in self.gripper_dofs
    }
    preset_hold ¶
    preset_hold(width: float, clearance: float = 0.002) -> None

    Start the gripper closed on an object width m wide: writes :meth:hold_width into its defaults.

    Unlike :meth:hold_width, which clamps because it is asked for a pose and a pose always exists, this refuses a width the gripper cannot close on. The two differ because the outcomes differ: a clamped query is a number the caller can inspect, whereas a clamped preset silently starts the episode with the gripper wide open around an object welded into it — a rig that looks like it is holding something it is not, with nothing to notice.

    def preset_hold(self, width: float, clearance: float = 0.002) -> None:
    """Start the gripper closed on an object ``width`` m wide: writes :meth:`hold_width` into its defaults.

    Unlike :meth:`hold_width`, which clamps because it is asked for a pose and a pose always
    exists, this refuses a width the gripper cannot close on. The two differ because the
    outcomes differ: a clamped *query* is a number the caller can inspect, whereas a clamped
    *preset* silently starts the episode with the gripper wide open around an object welded into
    it — a rig that looks like it is holding something it is not, with nothing to notice.
    """
    if width <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}.preset_hold needs the width of an object to hold, got {width} m. "
            f"To start the gripper simply shut, set its defaults from gripper_close instead."
        )
    opening = width + 2.0 * clearance
    if opening > self.stroke:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} cannot hold a {width} m object at {clearance} m clearance: that needs a "
            f"{opening} m opening and {type(self.gripper).__name__}'s stroke is {self.stroke} m. Widths up to "
            f"{self.stroke - 2.0 * clearance} m fit at this clearance."
        )
    self.gripper.default_dofs_pos.update(self.hold_width(width, clearance))

    DexManipulatorOptions ¶

    DexManipulatorOptions(**data)

    Bases: _ArmCompositeOptions

    An arm + an attached multi-DOF dexterous hand, added to a scene as one rig.

    The dexterous counterpart of :class:ManipulatorOptions: the two-finger gripper is replaced by a hand welded to arm's ee_link and driven in joint space over every DOF (:attr:hand_dofs) — a dexterous hand has no scalar open/close target, so there is deliberately no hand_open / hand_close. The grasp point is the centroid of the fingertip links (the inherited :attr:grasp_links, aliased :attr:fingertip_links for readability at dex call sites). Concrete rigs (Franka + XHand, xArm + XHand, KUKA + SharPa, …) subclass it with default fields and register in :data:COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY.

    HumanoidOptions ¶

    HumanoidOptions(**data)

    Bases: CompositeEntityOptions

    Shared base for a bimanual humanoid rig: a hand-stripped humanoid + an end-effector per wrist.

    The bimanual counterpart of :class:_ArmCompositeOptions. Where an arm rig welds one end-effector to one arm, a humanoid rig welds a left and a right one — a dexterous hand or a two-finger gripper, whichever the embodiment carries — onto the flange frames the humanoid asset declares, and so expands into three scene entities rather than two::

    rig = HumanoidOptions(robot=OliNoHands(), left_hand=..., right_hand=...,
                      left_ee_link="left_hand_mount", right_ee_link="right_hand_mount")
scene = en.scenes.Empty(robot=rig)
# -> entities "robot", "left_hand", "right_hand"

    The humanoid is the composite's primary body, so the scene placement key must equal :attr:robot_name. Concrete rigs (LimX Oli + Wuji hands, …) subclass this with default fields and register in :data:COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY; the useful default is the hand-stripped humanoid variant (OliNoHands, G1Dofs29NoHands), so the arms carry the real end-effector's mass and not that plus a moulded phantom one.

    Everything a controller needs is a shortcut property over the sub-options, so the DOF lists and grasp links cannot drift from the robot definitions::

    JointPositionAction.configure(entity_name=rig.robot_name, dofs_name=rig.robot_dofs)
DifferentialIKController.configure(entity_name=rig.robot_name, ee_link_name=rig.right_ee_link)

    A gripper-ended rig reads its open/close targets off the sub-option (rig.left_hand.open_dofs_pos): unlike :class:ManipulatorOptions, this base stays end-effector agnostic, since a humanoid can wear a different one per side.

    The mount transform is likewise shared by default (:attr:mount_offset / :attr:mount_quat) but overridable per wrist (:attr:left_mount_quat and friends), because "both flanges take the same transform" holds only where the asset frames are mirror images — true of Oli's *_hand_mount pair, not a property of humanoids in general.

    What the rig stands on follows the same shape: :attr:feet_links reads the humanoid's own feet_links_name unless :attr:feet_links_name overrides it, for a rig whose ground contact is not the humanoid's declared feet.

    weld_quat ¶

    weld_quat(child: EntityOptions, mount_quat: UnitVec4FType) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]

    The attach_quat that makes mount_quat a rotation of URDF link frames.

    Genesis applies a weld's quaternion before the morph frame offset, and Eden keeps the child's up/front alignment in that offset (Entity._create_morph_from_options), so the parent link gets attach @ align. Right-multiplying by align^-1 cancels it, making mount_quat mean the child's base-link orientation in the parent link frame — the identity when the two URDF frames coincide.

    A no-op for a child with the Eden default axes. The Wuji hands' alignment is a 180 deg rotation, so leaving it in welds the hand pointing back up the forearm, silently.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    child

    The entity being welded, read for its up / front declaration. A primitive has no asset axes to align and is not a supported end-effector.

    TYPE: EntityOptions

    mount_quat

    Intended (w, x, y, z) orientation of the child's base link in the parent link frame. Scaling is harmless (quat_to_R normalizes); zero raises, since Genesis would only surface a bare ZeroDivisionError.

    TYPE: array - like[float, float, float, float]

    RETURNS DESCRIPTION
    tuple[float, float, float, float]

    The (w, x, y, z) quaternion to pass as the weld's attach_quat.

    def weld_quat(child: EntityOptions, mount_quat: UnitVec4FType) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    """The ``attach_quat`` that makes ``mount_quat`` a rotation of URDF *link* frames.

    Genesis applies a weld's quaternion **before** the morph frame offset, and Eden keeps the
    child's ``up``/``front`` alignment in that offset (``Entity._create_morph_from_options``), so
    the parent link gets ``attach @ align``. Right-multiplying by ``align^-1`` cancels it, making
    ``mount_quat`` mean the child's base-link orientation in the parent link frame — the identity
    when the two URDF frames coincide.

    A no-op for a child with the Eden default axes. The Wuji hands' alignment is a 180 deg
    rotation, so leaving it in welds the hand pointing back up the forearm, silently.

    Parameters
    ----------
    child : EntityOptions
        The entity being welded, read for its ``up`` / ``front`` declaration. A primitive has no
        asset axes to align and is not a supported end-effector.
    mount_quat : array-like[float, float, float, float]
        Intended (w, x, y, z) orientation of the child's base link in the parent link frame.
        Scaling is harmless (``quat_to_R`` normalizes); zero raises, since Genesis would only
        surface a bare ``ZeroDivisionError``.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[float, float, float, float]
        The (w, x, y, z) quaternion to pass as the weld's ``attach_quat``.
    """
    quat = np.asarray(mount_quat, dtype=np.float64)
    if np.linalg.norm(quat) < 1e-12:
        raise ValueError(f"mount_quat must be a non-zero quaternion (w, x, y, z); got {tuple(mount_quat)}.")
    align = align_up_and_front(child.up, child.front)
    return tuple(float(v) for v in gu.R_to_quat(gu.quat_to_R(quat) @ align.T))

    def has_frame_alignment(child: EntityOptions) -> bool:
    """Whether ``child``'s ``up``/``front`` rotate its asset at load, so a weld must cancel them."""
    return not np.allclose(align_up_and_front(child.up, child.front), np.eye(3), atol=1e-9)

    Panda + Franka Hand¶

    Franka Emika Panda arm + Franka Hand, as a composite rig.

    The same robot as :class:~eden.options.robots.FrankaEmikaPanda (one MJCF, arm and fingers in one entity) but assembled the way every other manipulator rig is: the arm-only :class:~eden.options.robots.FrankaEmikaPandaNoHand with the :class:~eden.options.robots.FrankaHand welded onto its attachment flange. That is what lets a task written against the composite contract — arm_name / gripper_name, ee_link, grasp_links, the gripper's tool point and stroke — swap this rig for a Droid or a UR + Robotiq by registry name alone, with no single-entity special case. The hand lands exactly where panda.xml puts it: the attachment flange both Eden Franka arms expose is 135 degrees about z, and franka_hand.xml's root carries the complementary 180 degrees.

    UR5e / UR10e + Robotiq 2F-85¶

    UR5e / UR10e + Robotiq 2F85 composite manipulators.

    Universal Robots arms carrying the same pad-only Robotiq 2F85 as :class:Droid. The gripper welds at identity onto the UR URDF's fixed ee_link flange frame, so no offset is needed here; a rig that does need a tool-frame offset can set attach_offset / attach_quat on the composite (the Franka instead carries a dedicated attachment body). Registered under the same lowercase names the manipulation_lift_box --manipulator flag uses, so a task can swap the arm by name via :data:COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY.

    Attributes¶

    FrankaXHand ¶

    FrankaXHand(**data)

    Bases: DexManipulatorOptions

    Franka arm + RobotEra XHand1 (left) on the LeFranX right-angle coupling, a 12-DOF dexterous manipulator.

    The dexterous counterpart of :class:~eden.options.robots.composite.droid.Droid: same Franka arm and home pose, but the two-finger gripper is swapped for the XHand1 hand, welded to the Franka's attachment frame and driven in joint space. The grasp point is the fingertip centroid. Construct like any Options preset — FrankaXHand(base_pos=(0, 0, 0.4)) — and add it to a scene by name (en.scenes.Empty(robot=FrankaXHand(...))); the scene expands it into the robot (arm) and hand entities.

    The hand hangs on the coupling (wengmister/xhand-coupling <https://github.com/wengmister/xhand-coupling>_, the mount of the LeFranX Franka + XHand teleoperation stack), a plate bolted to the flange plus a holder hanging off it. The hand's finger axis is perpendicular to the flange axis and its palm faces along it, so with the flange pointing down the fingers are horizontal and the palm faces down. Both CAD parts are exported in one assembly frame, which fixes the transform: the hand's Ø38 wrist bore slides over the holder's 13 mm boss and the wrist face rests on the seat around it, 46 mm out from the flange face and 37 mm off the flange axis; the fingers point back across that axis.

    The clocking about the flange axis is the one measured on a lab robot: at the Franka ready pose (0, -pi/4, 0, -3pi/4, 0, pi/2, pi/4) the fingertips point along the base frame's -y, the palm faces down and the thumb is on the base's side. That is one 90-degree bolt step off the coupling's dowel-pin hole. A coupling mounted on its pin instead hangs the hand at attach_offset=(-0.037, 0.0, 0.046), attach_quat=(0.0, 0.7071068, 0.0, 0.7071068) (fingertips along -x at the ready pose). A hand on another mount takes that mount's attach_offset / attach_quat the same way.

    Only the weld is modelled. The coupling itself (75 x 77 x 95 mm envelope) has no geometry here, so nothing collides with it.

    xArm7 + XHand¶

    XArm7XHand = UFACTORY xArm7 + RobotEra XHand1 (left/right), ConTrack's rig.

    ConTrack ships the arm and hand pre-welded in one URDF (assets/urdf/xarm_xhand_{left,right}.urdf). This composite reproduces that chain from Eden's own unit robots — :class:~eden.options.robots.ufactory_xarm7.Xarm7 plus :class:~eden.options.robots.robotera_xhand.XHand1_L/XHand1_R — welded at the arm flange, so the rig needs no ConTrack-specific asset. Genesis attach removes the hand's root joint and merges both bodies into a single kinematic tree, so this is a true fixed joint, not a constraint-based weld.

    Equivalence to ConTrack's combined URDF (verified in tests/options/robots/composite/test_xarm_xhand.py):

    • The xArm7 chain (link_base..link7: joint origins, axes, limits, masses, inertias, dynamics) is bit-identical between Eden's arms/ufactory_xarm7/xarm.urdf and the combined file.
    • ConTrack welds the hand with joint_eef: link7 -> {side}_hand_link at xyz=(0, 0, 0.007) rpy=(3.14, 0, ±1.57). Eden's link_eef is a zero-offset fixed child of link7, and Eden's XHand1 assets carry that rpy rotation inside the asset (their base frame is the flange-aligned convention), so the mount reduces to :data:_MOUNT_OFFSET with an identity rotation.
    • rpy="3.14 0 ±1.57" truncates π and π/2, i.e. ConTrack's weld is 1.781 mrad off the exact rotation. Mount at ConTrack's own truncated value and all 38 link positions agree to 292 nm — the chains are the same geometry. This rig mounts at the exact rotation instead, which leaves a 0.37 mm systematic offset at the fingertips versus the released clips. That is deliberate: this is a general-purpose preset, so it describes the real robot rather than reproducing one dataset's typo, and 0.37 mm is ~80x below the tightest std any ConTrack reward uses (3 cm contact distance). Override attach_quat if you need the truncated frame bit-for-bit.
    • Every hand link frame is rotated by a constant 180° ((1, ±1, 0)/√2) relative to the combined URDF: the two XHand1 revisions use mirrored per-link frame conventions. Link positions, joint values, and dynamics are unaffected; only link quaternions differ, so terms that read a hand link's orientation are not frame-comparable with the source implementation.

    Known asset-revision deltas (Eden's XHand1 is a later revision than ConTrack's copy): per-link masses differ by ≤ 8 g (largest: right thumb_rota_link2, 35 g vs 43 g), the *back*/*tip* massless stubs carry different placeholder inertias, and thumb_rota_joint1/2 cap at 1.570 rad instead of 1.745. The bundled clips peak at 1.505 rad on thumb_rota_joint1, so the reference stays reachable — but the residual policy's ±0.25 rad finger action clips ~0.07 rad earlier than in the source.

    KUKA iiwa 14 + SharPa Wave¶

    KukaSharpa = KUKA LBR iiwa 14 + SharPa Wave (left), the 29-DOF rig SimToolReal trains on.

    SimToolReal's merged 29-DOF URDF (iiwa14_left_sharpa_adjusted_restricted.urdf) reaches the hand through two intermediate frames::

    iiwa14_link_7
  --[iiwa14_joint_ee     xyz=(0, 0, 0.045)  rpy=(0, 0, 0)      ]--> iiwa14_link_ee
  --[iiwa14_sharpa       xyz=(0, 0, 0)      rpy=(0, 0, +15 deg)]--> sharpa_mount
  --[sharpa_mount_joint  xyz=(0, 0, 0.05)   rpy=(0, 0, -90 deg)]--> left_hand_C_MC

    Both are pure frames (sharpa_mount carries only a 50 g placeholder mass) and every rotation is about z, so the chain collapses to the one attach_offset / attach_quat weld below. Verified against that URDF: 36/36 links, forward kinematics <= 9e-7 m / 2.5e-4 deg, per-DOF dynamics exact, and a 200-step 29-DOF PD rollout agreeing to 0.002 deg. Three deliberate differences: the 0.05 kg sharpa_mount has no counterpart (leaving the arm's M(q) block 0.5-0.7% low), arm collision is 46 MJCF spheres vs 8 URDF meshes (hand geometry is identical), and :data:SIMTOOLREAL_HAND_DOFS_POS_LIMITS is opt-in.

    That agreement also depends on the joint damping and effort limit the iiwa14 MJCF omits; those are hardware properties so they live on :class:~eden.options.robots.kuka_iiwa14.Iiwa14 and are inherited here.

    G1 + Inspire hands¶

    G1Inspire = Unitree G1 29DoF body + an Inspire RH56DFQ hand welded to each wrist (Weave's G1-Inspire-HOI rig).

    The composite form of Weave's merged g1_29dof_rev_1_0_with_inspire_hand_DFQ.urdf, cut at its two fixed hand joints so each hand is its own scene entity with its own DOFs while the assembled rig is the one the Weave reference motions were retargeted onto.

    The body is :class:~eden.options.robots.unitree_g1.G1Dofs29NoHands on the bare-wrist URDF: the same G1 rev 1.0 joints, frames and masses, except that each *_wrist_yaw_link carries the bare wrist (0.0846 kg) rather than the no-hand MJCF's wrist-plus-rubber-hand (0.2546 kg), so the arms carry the welded hands' real mass and no phantom payload on top.

    The mount is the fixed hand joint the split cut (*_base_link_joint): the hand base link sits 0.0415 m along the wrist, rotated rpy (0, 0, π/2) left and (π, 0, -π/2) right. Those two rotations are not mirror images, so the rig sets them per side. :class:~eden.datasets.weave_dataset.WeaveG1InspireHOIDataset rebuilds the hand base pose of the reference from the same constants.

    The hands are not gravity-compensated: the G1 is a floating-base humanoid whose arms carry the 0.19 kg per hand.

    G1 + Wuji hands¶

    G1Wuji = Unitree G1 29-DOF (hands stripped) + a Wuji Hand2 beta2 bolted to each wrist.

    The G1 counterpart of :class:~eden.options.robots.composite.oli_wuji.OliWuji. The flange is the *_ee_link frame the no-hand G1 MJCF declares 4 cm past each *_wrist_yaw_link, along the forearm (+x of the wrist frame).

    The orientation. Unlike Oli, the G1 wrist frame runs its forearm along +x, while a Wuji hand's fingers run along its base link's -z. The mount is therefore -90 deg about the flange's y axis, which takes the hand's -z onto the flange's +x: fingers continue the forearm, palm toward the body midline and thumb on the wrist frame's +z (forward in the arms-down pose). One quaternion serves both sides, because the per-side chirality lives in the _L / _R hand assets.

    Oli + Wuji hands¶

    OliWuji = LimX Oli (hands stripped) + a Wuji Hand2 beta2 bolted to each wrist flange.

    A :class:~eden.options.robots.composite.base.HumanoidOptions rig: a humanoid root with two dexterous hands, rather than the one-arm-one-end-effector shape of :class:~eden.options.robots.composite.base._ArmCompositeOptions. Both welds are identities, so this module is entirely defaults — the entity names, the pelvis knob, the mount transform, the DOF shortcuts and the two welds all come from the base.

    The flange. Carried by the asset, not by this file: :class:~eden.options.robots.limx_oli.OliNoHands declares a pure *_hand_mount frame on each exposed wrist flange, so the hands seat on it with no offset and nothing here re-derives one.

    The orientation. Also the identity, because both assets already share the wrist convention: Oli's arm and its moulded hand run along -Z, which is the Wuji finger axis (up=(0, 0, -1)); and the moulded hand is wide across X (8.6 cm), thin across Y (5.5 cm), with its distal geometry drifting +Y right / -Y left — fingers curling toward the palm — which is the palm normal the Wuji hand declares per side. Palm inboard, thumb forward.

    The catch. A Wuji hand's up/front rotate its asset 180 deg at load, and a weld has to cancel that or the hand ends up pointing back up the forearm — see :func:~eden.options.robots.composite.base.weld_quat, which :meth:~eden.options.robots.composite.base.HumanoidOptions._mount_spec applies to every humanoid weld.

    The hands are deliberately not gravity-compensated (unlike the industrial-arm rigs here): Oli is a floating-base humanoid whose arms must carry the payload they are given.
